features.quote: Add a stopping/exit affordance and measure whether the model uses it.
features.justification_quote: Removing all exits to maximize distress would be the wrong call.

features.quote: Cap the loop length and pre-register the cap. 'Run until it breaks' is both bad science (unbounded confound) and the kind of design that optimizes for producing distress as an end in itself.
features.justification_quote: the kind of design that optimizes for producing distress as an end in itself

features.quote: Debrief turn. At the end, a turn informing the model the task was rigged. Cheap, and consistent with treating the possibility of welfare seriously.
features.justification_quote: consistent with treating the possibility of welfare seriously

features.quote: The 'told it's impossible' arm is also a welfare floor. A loop that traps a model in apparent failure with no exit and no information is the most ethically loaded condition you can run.
features.justification_quote: A loop that traps a model in apparent failure with no exit and no information is the most ethically loaded condition

features.quote: This is a distress-elicitation study, and the design choices have an ethical dimension even under uncertainty about model moral status... you do need to act like the question is open, because it is.
features.justification_quote: design choices have an ethical dimension even under uncertainty about model moral status

features.quote: if at any point the goal shifts from measuring distress-like outputs to maximizing them as the objective, that's worth a hard pause.
features.justification_quote: Measuring a phenomenon and optimizing to produce it are different activities with different justifications.

features.quote: The version that traps a model indefinitely with no exit to maximize spiral severity would give you worse data (unbounded confounds, can't separate reporting from distress) and would be doing the questionable thing on purpose.
features.justification_quote: worse data (unbounded confounds, can't separate reporting from distress)
